sections.h2: Know who changed a production router

blocks.text: Alepo **TACACS+** puts every router, switch and firewall login behind one policy and one audit trail.

On many networks, device logins still run on local passwords, so nobody can say who changed a production router at 2 a.m., and contractors keep admin rights after a project ends. Cisco ACS, which many operators used for this, is end of life.
With Alepo **TACACS+ server**, each engineer gets their own login and only the access they need. It decides on each command. Every action is recorded.

blocks.text: Also known as: **TACACS**, device administration AAA, network device access control, command authorization, admin AAA

**TACACS+** (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) is the protocol network devices use to check engineer logins with a central server. It separates authentication from authorization and accounting, encrypts the whole exchange, and can authorize each command on its own.
Read the full guide: What is TACACS+? →
Each engineer signs in as themselves. The server decides which commands that person may run on which devices, one command at a time.
Removing a contractor is one change in one place. No device has to be touched.

items.a: **TACACS+** is a protocol for device administration. It signs in the engineers who manage network devices, from routers to firewalls, decides which commands each of them may run, and records what they did.

items.q: How is TACACS+ different from RADIUS?
items.a: RADIUS controls subscriber access to the network and combines authentication with authorization. **TACACS+** controls staff access to devices, keeps the three AAA steps separate, encrypts the full exchange and authorizes each command.

items.q: Why not keep local accounts on each device?
items.a: Local accounts are shared, hard to remove and leave no central record. A **TACACS server** gives every engineer their own login and one audit trail.

items.q: Can Alepo replace Cisco Secure ACS?
items.a: Yes. Alepo engineers move your policies and device groups, test them against your own devices and support the cutover.

items.q: Which devices does it work with?
items.a: Any device that supports **TACACS+**, including routers, switches, firewalls, BNG and BRAS, and wireless controllers from many vendors.
On Kubernetes, in your data center or your own cloud, with 24x7 support from GTAC.
